Hmm, I'll check if it's hung by any chance hivetests2.ethdevops.io oh, I think we should update Nethermind image here 🙂 Yeah same with geth, we're looking into pushing the update <@758579010027782144> Are you coming to the merge discussion? It's happening right now No, I had to return to Poland 😦 sorry everyone timeouts -> we have a timeout now for newPayload (of course, we can remove it) and also a general timeout for RPC calls latestValidHash -> whatever will work for other EL will be fine for Nethermind. However, I think it is super important to have hive tests for it and also to have hive tests during the sync when we sync with an invalid chain (I discussed it with <@892053833121923094> ) payloadAttributes -> timestamp check. We can do option 1, so like geth now its processing slots properly, its taking time to sync up the epoch summaries now <@758579010027782144> What were your issues/points to discuss wrt syncing How long does it take for CL to send the tip of the chain? If I understand things correctly, EL couldn't start state sync before CL is close to the head. Let's say, we're using checkpoint sync, so we have ~2 weeks old checkpoint. We're starting fresh sync (CL + EL). CL will start sending us requests one by one from checkpoint, so we will have ~100k requests I've overridden the TTD to `47101300000000000000000`, this is to account for varying hashrate on mainnet since the configs were created last week. We estimate that TTD should be hit at ~10AM tomorrow, huge props to <@686695036733227017> for his help! 😄 It makes very little sense to use checkpoint sync and not just start from the current finalized state. So basically you wind up close to the end immediately. You will normally get <100 new blocks from the CL one-by-one. Its more challenging with a node that has been offline for a few days - then it is going to switch to optimistic mode and send you a lot of blocks at once. I suspect ELs will want to optimise the handling of newPayload and fcu calls when they know they're already syncing to do as little as possible and possibly even discard redundant fcu updates (ie if the CL sends 3 fcu updates that you have in a queue, immediately respond SYNCING to the first two and only actually process the third). Similarly, CLs may wind up limiting fcu calls a bit during sync, particularly if they know they have a whole batch of blocks to import. Not much we can do about newPayload though. We are not sending fcu sequentially on block batches what's the perf overhead of newPayload+fcu over just newPayload? on the EL side newPayload + fcu might even be faster okay, so if we get <100 new blocks during fresh sync is not a problem at all, thx! Mario can't post in this channel, but he sent me this to track when TTD is hit for the shadow fork: https://bordel.wtf/
